NOTICE OF PUBLIC HEARING AND AGENDA
NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS
Tuesday, April 11, 2023
ONE OR MORE SUPERVISORS MAY ATTEND VIA VIDEO AND/OR TELEPHONICALLY 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors will hold a meeting open to the public on Tuesday, April 11, 2023, in the Supervisors’
Chamber in the Navajo County Governmental Complex, 100 East Code Talkers Drive, Holbrook, Arizona. The Board may vote to
meet in a closed executive session to discuss certain matters and for legal advice on any item as indicated on the following
agenda, pursuant to A.R.S. § 38-431.03(A) (3). 
The Navajo County Board of Supervisors finds that it is in the best interest of the community to conduct this public meeting using
a hybrid method in order to serve the public interest. 
Join Zoom Meeting, click here: https://us06web.zoom.us/j/87692173340?pwd=WDU3WWhlZFcxd1JqN1BzYXI1dUdpZz09 
 
Call In Number: 1-253-215-8782 OR 1-346-248-7799 (You may use either teleconference number)
Meeting ID: 876 9217 3340
Passcode: 271616
Persons with disabilities who need accommodation to attend or participate in the meeting may contact the Clerk of the Board’s
office at (928) 524-4053; at least 48 hours prior to the meeting, so an accommodation can be arranged.
Items on the agenda may be considered out of order at the Chairman’s discretion. A copy of the agenda background material
provided to the Board, except items to be considered in executive session, is available for public inspection at Navajo County
website, www.navajocountyaz.gov
“NOTICE TO PARENTS AND LEGAL GUARDIANS: Parents and legal guardians have the right to consent before Navajo County makes a video
or voice recording of a minor child, pursuant to A.R.S. § 1-602(A)(9). The Navajo County Board of Supervisors regular meetings are recorded and
may be viewed on Navajo County’s website, and social media pages. If you permit your child to attend/participate in a televised Navajo County
Board of Supervisors meeting, a recording will be made, and your child’s picture may be posted on Navajo County’s social media pages. You may
exercise your right not to consent by not allowing your child to attend/participate in the meeting.” 
9:00 a.m. Call To Order: Invocation and Pledge of Allegiance
           
1. CALL TO THE PUBLIC: Individuals may address the Board on any relevant issue for up to
3 minutes. At the close of the call to the public, Board members may not respond to any
comments but may respond to criticism, ask staff to review a matter or ask that a matter be
placed on a future agenda.
 
 
2. CONSENT AGENDA: These items are considered to be routine or administrative in nature
and will be approved in a single motion. A Board member may request for any item to be
removed from the consent agenda and considered on the regular agenda:
 
 
a. Minutes: March 28, 2023  
 
b. Warrant & Voucher Report over $1000, March 2023  
 
c. Constable Reports: Pinetop-Lakeside Precinct #6, March 2023

<!-- page 2 -->
d. Sympathy Letters: Cindy Allen (Assessor), Sophia Descheeny (Assessor), Robert LaForm
(Assessor), the family of Greg Green (Public Defender), and the family of Vickie Sutton
(Sheriiff's Office)
 
 
e. Re-Appointment of Jon H. Saline as a Judge Pro Tempore to serve in the Superior Court in
Navajo County for a term beginning July 1, 2023 and ending June 30, 2024
 
 
f. Appointment of Tabitha Stickel as a new LWDB member to represent Adult Ed under WIOA
Title II
 
 
g. Appointment of Ryleigh Aubuchon, AZDES Program Manager Workforce Development
Administration, as a new LWDB member to fulfill our Wagner Peyser Representative
 
 
h. Appointment of Rochelle Shanta, AZDES Title III Rep, Local Workforce Supervisor  
 
i. Contracts signed by County Manager/Assistant County Manager pursuant to Board of
Supervisors Resolution: Professional Services Contract with JE Fuller Hydrology &
Geomorphology, Inc. for Navajo County ALERT System Maintenance and Improvements for
2023; Agreement with Strategic Government Resources, Inc. for Executive Recruitment
Services for County Manager position
 
 
j. Reissuance of Stale Dated Checks  
 
k. Tax exemptions filed pursuant to ARS §42-11153 as a Request for Redemption of Waiver  
 
l. Approval of 1 Back Tax Land parcel sold over the counter in the amount of $477.60  
 
m. FY 2024 TCPF Court Field Trainer Grant Application  
 
n. Approval of a new three-year contract with Microsoft for software services  
 
o. Amendment Number 1 extending Contract No. B20-02-014 with Ryan Rapp Underwood &
Pacheco, PLC. for one additional year (July 1, 2023, through June 30, 2024)
 
 
p. Approval of the Chicanos Por La Causa, Inc. Title 1B Budget Amendment A approved by the
Local Workforce Development Board March 22, 2023
 
 
q. Board Membership Requirements Waiver Request to the Workforce Administrative Council

<!-- page 3 -->
3. EMPLOYEE RECOGNITION:  
 
a. Presentation on the activities of the CARE Committee for 2022  
Presented By: Ron Smith
 
4. BOARD OF SUPERVISORS:  
 
a. Consideration of a Proclamation, proclaiming April 2023 as "National County Government
Month". 
 
Presented By: Chairman Peshlakai/Eric Scott
 
5. SHERIFF'S OFFICE:  
 
a. Consideration of a proclamation declaring the week beginning April 9th through April 15th,
2023 as "National Telecommunicators Week" in Navajo County, Arizona.
 
Presented By: Sheriff David Clouse
 
6. COUNTY ATTORNEY:  
 
a. Consideration of a Proclamation declaring April 2023 as "Navajo County Sexual Assault
Awareness Month".
 
Presented By: Roxanne Padilla
 
7. ADMINISTRATIVE SERVICES:  
 
a. Presentation to the 2023 winner of the Navajo County Iron Chef Challenge  
Presented By: Eric Scott
 
b. Consideration of Northern Arizona Care and Services after Assault (NACASA) request for
funding in collaboration with other community organizations to support the infrastructure in
the amount of $10,000 annually.
 
Presented By: Denise Burley
 
8. NAVAJO COUNTY PUBLIC HEALTH SERVICES DISTRICT: Board of Directors
Session: 
 
 
a. REGULAR AGENDA:  
 
1. Consideration of a Proclamation declaring April 2023 as "Public Health Month in Navajo
County".
 
Presented By: Janelle Linn

<!-- page 4 -->
2. Consideration of an Intergovernmental Agreement between Navajo County and County
Municipalities for the use of Opioid Settlement proceeds pursuant to the One Arizona Plan
and Opioid Settlement Agreement Funding Project Vetting Process.
 
Presented By: Janelle Linn
 
9. PUBLIC WORKS:  
 
a. Consideration of award of Contract Number B23-02-024, Supply of Aggregate for Cover
Material to Perkins Cinders Inc, Hatch Construction and Paving Inc, and Brimhall Sand
Rock and Building Materials, effective April 11, 2023, through April 10, 2024.
 
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
 
b. PLANNING & ZONNING:  
 
1. PUBLIC HEARING: Consideration of the adoption of Resolution Number 11-2023 
approving/denying a Special Use Permit to operate a recovery residential facility for ten
(10) residents with 13 staff per week with overlapping shifts.
 
Presented By: Cody Cooper
 
c. NAVAJO COUNTY FLOOD CONTROL DISTRICT: Board of Directors Session:  
 
1. CONSENT AGENDA: The following item(s) are considered to be of a routine or
administrative in nature and will be approved as a group unless a member of the Board
wishes to discuss a particular item: 
 
 
a. Amendment Number 1 to the Professional Services Agreement with The WLB Group, Inc.
for the Bourdon Ranch Road / Millet Swale Culvert Project
 
 
10. COUNTY BUSINESS UPDATE: Report from County Manager, County Attorney and
Board members.
 
 
 
11. ADJOURN  
 
Dated: April 7, 2023 NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS 
Posted: 1:35 p.m. By: MWB                         
Melissa W. Buckley - Clerk of the Board

Board of Supervisors Regular 2. m.        
Meeting Date: 04/11/2023  
Title: FY 2023 TCPF Court Field Trainer Grant Application 
Submitted By: Lu Ann Garbini, Court Administrator 
Department: Superior Court
Motion before the Board:
FY 2024 TCPF Court Field Trainer Grant Application 
Background:
The Court Field Trainer provides essential business processing, system support and on-site
training for all Navajo County Courts. 
A local Field Trainer saves the Courts and the County money by reducing travel costs. 
The funding source for this position is from the Court's local Fill the Gap (FTG) fund, Local
Judicial Collection Enhancement (JCEF) fund, Fines/Fees and Restitution Enforcement Program
(FARE) Operation expense reimbursement fees and the Supreme Court Field Trainer (TCPF)
Grant.
No general funds are requested. 
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: FY2024
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested: 0
Fiscal Impact:
State and local court funds. No general funds requested.

Title: Microsoft Annual Contract
Submitted For: Ken Dewitt, Information Technology Director 
Submitted By: Ken Dewitt, Information Technology Director
Department: Information Technology
Motion before the Board:
Approval of a new three-year contract with Microsoft for software services
Background:
Navajo County has been running Microsoft products for many years and has made a large
investment of time and training to provide a high level of support for the employees.  This
contract is for software that flows through the entire County from local PC operating systems,
Excel, and Word to the Servers that store all the data for the different Departments and Offices. 
This also includes opportunities to leverage Cloud services including email and storage in
Microsoft's secure government cloud. The chosen vendor is currently on State contract. 
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: 2023-2024
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested: 410,515.19
Fiscal Impact:
This is an annual amount that the County will pay for the next three years.  The total amount is
spread among all Departments and Offices.

2. Order requirements. 
a. Minimum order requirements.  
Qualified Users or Qualified Devices.  The initial order must include at least 250 Licenses for 
Enterprise Products or Enterprise Online Services. 
(i) Enterprise commitment.  Enrolled Affiliate must order enough Licenses to cover all 
Qualified Users or Qualified Devices, depending on the License Type, with one or more 
Enterprise Products or a mix of Enterprise Products and the corresponding Enterprise 
Online Services (as long as all Qualified Devices not covered by a License are only used 
by users covered with a user License). 
(ii) Enterprise Online Services only.  If no Enterprise Product is ordered, then Enrolled 
Affiliate need only maintain at least 250 Subscription Licenses for Enterprise Online 
Services. 
b. Additional Products.  Upon satisfying the minimum order requirements above, Enrolled 
Affiliate may order Additional Products.

more restrictive use rights than the version that is current at the start of the applicable initial or 
renewal term of the Enrollment, those more restrictive use rights will not apply to Enrolled 
hat term.

on its initial order and on any additional orders. 
e. Resellers.  Enrolled Affiliate must choose and maintain a Reseller authorized in the United 
States. Enrolled Affiliate will acquire its Licenses through its chosen Reseller. Orders must be 
submitted to the Reseller who will transmit the order to Microsoft. The Reseller and Enrolled 
Affiliate determine pricing and payment terms as between them, and Microsoft will invoice the 
Reseller based on those terms.

f. Adding Products. 
(i) Adding new Products not previously ordered.  New Enterprise Products or Enterprise 
Online Services may be added at any time by contacting a Microsoft Account Manager or

placed in the month the Product is first used.  For Additional Products that are Online

g. True-up requirements.  Enrolled Affiliate must submit an annual true-up order that accounts 
for any changes since the initial order or last order.  If there are no changes, then an update 
statement must be submitted instead of a true-up order. 
(i) Enterprise Products.  For Enterprise Products, Enrolled Affiliate must determine the 
number of Qualified Devices and Qualified Users (if ordering user-based Licenses) at the 
time the true-up order is placed and must order additional Licenses for all Qualified Devices 
and Qualified Users that are not already covered by existing Licenses, including any 
Enterprise Online Services. 
(ii) Additional Products.  For Additional Products that have been previously ordered under 
this Enrollment, Enrolled Affiliate must determine the maximum number of Additional 
Products used since the latter of the initial order, the last true-up order, or the prior 
anniversary date and submit a true-up order that accounts for any increase. 
(iii) Online Services.  For Online Services identified as eligible for true-up in the Product 
Terms, Enrolled Affiliate may place a reservation order for the additional Licenses prior to 
use and payment may be deferred until the next true-up order.  Microsoft will provide a 
report of Reserved Licenses ordered but not yet invoiced to Enrolled Affiliate and its 
Reseller.  Reserved Licenses will be invoiced retrospectively to the month in which they 
were ordered. 
(iv) Subscription License reductions.  Enrolled Affiliate may reduce the quantity of 
Subscription Licenses at the Enrollment anniversary date on a prospective basis if 
permitted in the Product Terms, as follows: 
1) For Subscription Licenses that are part of an Enterprise-wide purchase, Licenses may 
be reduced if the total quantity of Licenses and Software Assurance for an applicable 
group meets or exceeds the quantity of Qualified Devices and Qualified Users (if 
ordering user-based Licenses) identified on the Product Selection Form, and includes 
any additional Qualified Devices and Qualified Users added in any prior true-up orders.  
Step-up Licenses do not count towards this total count. 
2) For Enterprise Online Services that are not a part of an Enterprise-wide purchase, 
Licenses can be reduced as long as the initial order minimum requirements are 
maintained.

use of the applicable Subscription License will be cancelled.

Navajo County               
Proclamation 
 
NATIONAL COUNTY GOVERNMENT MONTH – April 2023 
“Counties RISE!” 
WHEREAS, counties RISE! through Resiliency, Inclusion, Solvency, and Empowerment; and  
WHEREAS, counties play an essential role in providing “people-centered” services by keeping Arizona’s 
communities safe and secure by preserving public health and well-being, ensuring public safety, and 
promoting local economies and resiliency; and  
WHEREAS, counties take seriously their leadership role in protecting and enhancing the health, welfare, 
and safety of citizens in the community and provide the tools to deliver more effective and higher 
quality services while containing costs through the efficient use of local tax dollars, with the goal to 
foster economic opportunities; and  
WHEREAS, with a broad range of responsibilities to residents, county governments uphold a mission to 
improve lives, strengthen communities, and foster civic engagement, by providing public health, justice, 
safety, infrastructure, transportation, technology, emergency management, and economic services that 
play a key role in every aspect from residents’ daily health to disaster response; and  
WHEREAS, there are fifteen counties in the State of Arizona responsible for and serving the needs of 
every resident of the State; and  
WHEREAS, Arizona counties reflect the wide diversity of people, culture, and landscape in our State; and  
WHEREAS, Navajo County will be hosting events throughout Navajo County to promote health and 
wellness to highlight April 2023 as Counties Health Month in accordance with “National County 
Government Month”.  
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT PROCLAIMED, by the Board of Supervisors of Navajo County that April of 2023 
is designated as “NATIONAL COUNTY GOVERNMENT MONTH” and encourage all county officials, 
employees, schools, and residents to participate in county government celebration activities. 
PASSED, ADOPTED AND APPROVED by the Board of Supervisors on April 11, 2023.

Board of Supervisors Regular 6. a.        
Meeting Date: 04/11/2023  
Title: Declaring April 2023 Sexual Assault Awareness Month
Submitted For: Brad Carlyon, County Attorney  Submitted By: Lynda Young, Office
Manager
Department: County Attorney
Presented By: Roxanne Padilla
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of a Proclamation declaring April 2023 as "Navajo County Sexual Assault
Awareness Month".
Background:
Sexual Assault Awareness month is observed in April every year in the United States, and it
aims to raise public awareness about sexual violence and its impact on survivors, families, and
communities. The origins of Sexual Assault Awareness month can be traced back to the 1970s
when women's rights activists started organizing events to raise awareness about the issue of
sexual violence.
In 1971, the Bay Area Women Against Rape opened as the nations first rape crisis center
offering immediate services to victims.  In 1975, the first national "Take Back the Night" march
was held in Philadelphia, which aimed to raise awareness about sexual assault and violence
against women. This event encouraged women to take a stand against sexual violence and to
reclaim their right to safety in public spaces.
In 2009, President Obama declared April as Sexual Assault Awareness Month.  Sexual Assault
Awareness Month provides an opportunity for survivors, advocates, and community members to
come together and raise awareness about sexual violence, promote prevention efforts, and show
support for survivors. It also serves as a reminder of the need to take action to end sexual
violence and support survivors in their healing journey.
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends acceptance and declaration of April as the 2023 Navajo County Sexual
Assault Awareness Month.

Navajo County      
   Proclamation 
 SEXUAL ASSAULT AWARENESS MONTH 
April 2023 
WHEREAS, 1 in 5 women in the United States experienced completed or attempted rape during their lifetime; and 
WHEREAS, nearly a quarter (24.8%) of men in the United States experienced some form of contact sexual violence in 
their lifetime; and 
WHEREAS, nationwide, 81% of women and 43% of men reported experiencing some form of sexual harassment and/or 
assault in their lifetime; and 
WHEREAS, one in three female victims of completed or attempted rape experienced it for the first time between the ages 
of 11 and 17; and  
WHEREAS, about one in four male victims of completed or attempted rape first experienced it between the ages of 11 
and 17; and 
WHEREAS, it is estimated that 734,630 people were raped (including threatened, attempted, or completed rape) in the 
U.S. in 2018; and 
WHEREAS, 40% of rapes and sexual assaults were reported to police in 2017, but only 25% were reported to police in 
2018; and 
WHEREAS, between 2% and 10% are false reports; and 
WHEREAS, 51.1% of female victims of rape reported being raped by an intimate partner and 40.8% by an acquaintance; 
and 
WHEREAS, 52.4% of male victims of rape reported being raped by an acquaintance and 15.2% by a stranger; and 
WHEREAS, our County has a moral obligation to work to prevent sexual assault and to address its brutal and destructive 
effects; and 
NOW THEREFORE, the Navajo County Board of Supervisors, do hereby proclaim the month of April 2023 as “Sexual 
Assault Awareness Month” and call on all Navajo County citizens to speak out against sexual assault and support local 
efforts to assist victims of these crimes in finding the help and healing they need. 
PASSED, ADOPTED AND APPROVED by the Board of Supervisors on April 11, 2023.

Board of Supervisors Regular 7. b.        
Meeting Date: 04/11/2023  
Title: NACASA Program Request for Funding
Submitted By: Leah Thomas, Deputy Clerk of the Board of Supervisors
Department: Administrative Services
Presented By: Denise Burley
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of Northern Arizona Care and Services after Assault (NACASA) request for
funding in collaboration with other community organizations to support the infrastructure in the
amount of $10,000 annually.
Background:
Northern Arizona Care And Services after Assault (NACASA) was established in 2002 to
respond to the emotional, physical, medical, and criminal justice needs of sexual assault victims.
It was originally established with the intention of developing the program into a free-standing
facility in Coconino County; however, it was unable to financially sustain its operation. In 2007,
North Country HealthCare and key community funding partners Coconino County, the City of
Flagstaff, and Flagstaff Medical Center came together to commit resources and a structure for
the continued operation of NACASA. By siting NACASA at North Country HealthCare
(NCHC), the service provision was able to increase in scope and size while leveraging clinical
capacities, expertise, facilities, pharmaceutical access, and the Community Health Center (CHC)
model to reduce barriers to care. The success and longevity of the NACASA program is the
result of the valued partnerships listed above. North Country HealthCare and NACASA are
well positioned to continue to provide these integral services that are a community benefit;
however, as the program grows, we need continued assistance from our partners to ensure
sustainability.
NACASA secured grant funding to begin providing medical forensic exams to victims of sexual
assault and domestic violence strangulation in Navajo and Apache Counties in 2019.  NACASA
now has three sites located in North Country HealthCare’s brick and mortar clinics in Holbrook,
Show Low, and Round Valley. We have partnered with the Navajo County Attorney’s Office,
the Family Advocacy Center, social service providers, as well as law enforcement throughout
the county. Our staff regularly attend the monthly MDT, SART, and Domestic Violence
Coalition meetings in Snowflake.
Program costs have increased substantially. From 2016 to November 2022, NACASA
compensated examiners a flat rate of $375 per exam. Effective mid-November 2022, this rate
was increased to $425 in accordance with inflation and cost of living increases for examiners.
Additionally, there was a need to recognize the administrative tasks and responsibilities of
examiners outside of exam/charting time, and therefore, examiners now receive an hourly rate to
attend to these tasks and participate in meetings and training.
There are also operating costs to manage the program including, but not limited to:

<!-- page 610 -->
Program Manager salary and employee related expenses
Travel throughout the service area
Supplies and equipment
Dedicated office space at the NCHC 4th St Clinic
A dedicated Forensic Electronic Health Record
Training
Outreach and education materials
Clinical oversight and credentialing/privileging
From FY19-21, Navajo County cases accounted for 16% of exams performed by the NACASA
program. In FY22, the percentage increased substantially to 21.5% of cases. These percentages
do not include federal, tribal, or non-report cases not assigned to a county, that together in FY22
averaged approximately 25% (24 exams) of total exams performed; however, most of these
cases occurred in Navajo and Coconino Counties.
Currently, NACASA has an existing Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) with Coconino
County, City of Flagstaff, and Northern Arizona Healthcare and commitments of annual funding
to assist with operational costs of the program.  North Country is seeking funding at low levels
from partners throughout the service area to achieve program sustainability.
Recommendation: 
NACASA is requesting a contract to provide funding, in collaboration with other community
organizations, to support the infrastructure of NACASA at an annual rate of $10,000, in
quarterly installments of $2,500.

Board of Supervisors Regular 8. a. 1.        
Meeting Date: 04/11/2023  
Title: Public Health Month April 2023 Proclamation
Submitted For: Janelle Linn, Health Director 
Submitted By: Janelle Linn, Health Director
Department: NC Public Health Services District
Presented By: Janelle Linn
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of a Proclamation declaring April 2023 as "Public Health Month in Navajo
County".
Background:
April is a month dedicated to numerous public health day, month or week observances.  
World Take Down Tobacco Day - April 1, 2023
World Health Day - April 7, 2023
National Healthcare Decisions Day - April 16, 2023
Public Health Week - April 3 -9, 2023
World Immunization Week & National Infant Immunization Week - April 24 - 30, 2023
Minority Health Month - Month of April
Alcohol Awareness Month - Month of April
Parkinson's Disease Awareness Month - Month of April
Autism Acceptance Month - April, 2023
Donate Life Month - April 2023
National Child Abuse Prevention Month - Month of April
Month of the Young Child - Month of April
Therefore, rather than bringing forward multiple proclamations, we're approaching the board to
declare April 2023 as Public Health Month in Navajo County, recognizing all of the various
health observances under the public health umbrella.
Recommendation: 
Recommend proclaiming April 2023 as Public Health Month in Navajo County.

Navajo County               
Proclamation 
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
PUBLIC HEALTH MONTH 2023 
WHEREAS, the public health field is grounded in fundamental truth that we as a society, we are united in evidence-based life-saving 
work to keep individuals and communities healthy and safe; and 
WHEREAS, public health professionals have been shaping our country for the better since the late 1700’s and the American Public 
Health Association was founded in 1872, at a time when scientific advances were helping to reveal the causes of communicable 
disease, laying the foundation for the public health infrastructure in place today.  From expanding access to immunizations, improving 
safety standards for food, traffic, healthy workplaces, to advocating for cleaner air and water, public health professionals have 
improved the lives of Americans, making our country stronger, healthier and more prosperous; and 
WHEREAS U.S. life expectancy has decreased in recent years and the three-year drop represents the longest sustained decline in 
lifespan expectancy since the Great Recession; further, studies consistently show the United States has a notably lower life 
expectancy than comparable countries; and 
WHEREAS, there is a significant difference in health status, such as obesity, poor mental health and substance use among people 
living in rural areas compared with people living in urban areas, and this variance increases because rural residents are often more 
likely to face social determinants that negatively impact health, such as poverty issues, access to healthcare barriers, and lack of 
economic opportunity; and 
WHEREAS, public health professionals help communities prevent, prepare for, withstand and recover from the impact of a full range 
of health threats, including disease outbreaks natural disasters, disasters caused by human activity, and health issues escalated by 
social impacts; and 
WHEREAS, public health action, together with scientific and technological advances, has plays a major role in reducing and in some 
cases, eliminating the spread of infectious disease, and in establishing today’s disease surveillance and control systems; and 
WHEREAS, 60 percent of Americans live with a preventable chronic disease, and health risks such as substance misuse, obesity, 
tobacco use, and mental illness are the primary reasons for 7 of every 10 deaths annually in the United States; and 
WHEREAS, looking forward Navajo County chooses to seize the opportunity to better prepare ourselves for the future and to build a 
stronger public health system throughout our county, making it a healthier and more resilient community; and 
WHEREAS, The Board of Supervisors would like to officially recognize the hard work and dedication of all those involved in improving the 
health status of individuals and communities, through public health initiatives, interventions, education and support; including healthcare 
providers, public health workers, and most of all, the citizens themselves for accepting responsibility for their personal health and striving to 
improve it. 
 
NOW, THEREFORE, BE IT PROCLAIMED, by the Board of Supervisors of Navajo County that April of 2023 is designated as 
“PUBLIC HEALTH MONTH 2023” in Navajo County. 
 
PASSED, ADOPTED AND APPROVED by the Board of Supervisors on APRIL 11, 2023. 
 
         ____________________________ 
Alberto Peshlakai, Chairman

Board of Supervisors Regular 8. a. 2.        
Meeting Date: 04/11/2023  
Title: Opioid Settlement Agreement County Municipalities IGA & Project Funding
Vetting Process
Submitted For: Janelle Linn, Health Director 
Submitted By: Janelle Linn, Health Director
Department: NC Public Health Services District
Presented By: Janelle Linn
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of an Intergovernmental Agreement between Navajo County and County
Municipalities for the use of Opioid Settlement proceeds pursuant to the One Arizona Plan and
Opioid Settlement Agreement Funding Project Vetting Process.
Background:
Navajo County and the municipalities in Navajo County are parties of the One Arizona Plan. 
This IGA, (MOU) details how settlement monies will be utilized collaboratively and
cooperatively, in a way to best benefit the residents of Navajo County and it's municipalities to
remediate the impact of opioid in their respective regions. The MOU centralizes funding and
reporting requirements to relieve the municipalities of separate reporting and individual project
implementation of public health interventions. The IGA outlines the joint exercise of powers
through creation of a steering committee, committee membership, and advisory members of the
committee. The MOU outlines the Guiding Principles & Core Abatement Strategies, developed
by Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health, to be utilized by the steering committee
as their guide for reviewing projects to bring before the Navajo County Board of Supervisors
for consideration for funding. The MOU has gone before the various municipality counsels and
been approved.
The proposed project vetting process for projects to be considered for funding ensures projects
meet the guiding principles and core abatement strategies outlined in the MOU. It ensures a fair
and transparent process to determine where to spend funding, that funding is spent on
evidence-based approaches, and that funding is spent responsibly, on those most impacted by
the opioid epidemic.
 
Recommendation: 
Recommending approval of IGA and funding project vetting process.

1 
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
INTERGOVERNMENTAL AGREEMENT FOR THE USE OF  
OPIOID SETTLEMENT PROCEEDS PURSUANT TO THE ONE ARIZONA PLAN 
 
THIS AGREEMENT is made and entered into on the effective date set forth below by 
and between Navajo County, a political subdivision of the State of Arizona (the “County”), and 
the CITY OF WINSLOW, a municipal corporation of the State of Arizona, the TOWN OF 
PINETOP-LAKESIDE, a municipal corporation of the State of Arizona, the CITY OF 
HOLBROOK, a municipal corporation of the State of Arizona, the CITY OF SHOW LOW, a 
municipal corporation of the State of Arizona, the TOWN OF SNOWFLAKE, a municipal 
corporation of the State of Arizona, and the TOWN OF TAYLOR, a municipal corporation of 
the State of Arizona (all hereinafter collectively referred to as the “Principals” or “Parties” or 
individually as “Principal” or “Party”). 
RECITALS 
WHEREAS, each of the parties hereto are also parties to that certain Memorandum of 
Understanding (MOU) between the State of Arizona, each of the fifteen Arizona counties, and all 
of the State’s municipalities which created the “One Arizona Plan” (attached hereto and 
incorporated herein as “Exhibit A”); and 
WHEREAS, the referenced MOU creates a plan for the distribution of certain settlement proceeds 
between the State, Counties, and Municipalities throughout the State of Arizona that have or may 
come from ongoing multi-state litigation in the federal courts related to the ongoing opioid crisis; 
and 
WHEREAS, the tribally controlled areas within Navajo County are separately negotiating a 
settlement with opioid manufacturers, distributors and retailers that meet the specific needs of 
tribal governments, and 
WHEREAS, the MOU provides detailed information about how the settlement proceeds that 
come from the “One Arizona Plan” may be utilized by the State, Counties and Municipalities 
throughout the State of Arizona; and 
WHEREAS, the MOU provides detailed reporting requirements for documenting how settlement 
monies are utilized once received by the various recipient jurisdictions and to monitor 
compliance, and 
WHEREAS, the MOU allows for coordination and cooperation between Navajo County and the 
municipalities located therein in determining how the resources received as a result of the One 
Arizona Plan may best be utilized to benefit the residents of the County and municipalities to 
remediate the impact of opioids in their respective regions; and 
WHEREAS, the MOU provides that the various county health departments throughout the State 
are charged with reporting requirements as to how settlement proceeds are utilized by the County 
and municipalities within the County, and

<!-- page 630 -->
2 
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
WHEREAS, the parties to this Agreement believe the mutual coordination and cooperation 
regarding the use of opioid settlement proceeds is in the best interests of the citizens of the 
County and municipalities and further desire to centralize reporting requirements so as to relieve 
the municipalities of reporting separately to the County Health Department, and 
WHEREAS, the governmental entities that are parties to this Agreement have authority to enter 
into the Agreement pursuant to A.R.S. § 11-952(A) and 9-240, 
NOW THEREFORE, the Parties to this Agreement hereby resolve to act jointly and 
cooperatively consistent with their independent authority to create the Navajo County Opioid 
Settlement Steering Committee that will coordinate with the Navajo County Public Health 
Services District in identifying priorities and projects to remediate the opioid crisis throughout 
Navajo County on non-tribal lands. 
COVENANTS 
1.)  JOINT EXERCISE OF POWERS AND CREATION OF STEERING 
COMMITTEE 
 
The parties hereto are jointly exercise their powers to create the Navajo County Opioid 
Settlement Steering Committee (hereafter “Committee”).   The Committee will be 
charged with working with the Navajo County Public Health Services District and have 
responsibility for identifying and recommending projects that help to remediate the 
opioid crisis throughout the County in both municipal and non-municipal areas of the 
County consistent with the “One Arizona Plan.”  The parties hereto understand that the 
ultimate responsibility for approving how settlement monies are spent lies with the 
governing board of the Navajo County Public Health Services District. 
 
2.) COMMITTEE MEMBERSHIP 
 
The Committee shall consist of the following voting members 
 
1.)  A representative from the City of Show Low to represent municipal interests 
throughout the County; 
2.) A representative from the City of Winslow to represent municipal interests 
throughout the County; 
3.) A representative of the Navajo County Sheriff’s Office; 
4.) A representative of the Navajo County Attorney’s Office; 
5.) The Director of the Navajo County Public Health Services District. 
The Committee shall be chaired by the Director of the Navajo County Public Health 
Services District.   A quorum of the Board shall be necessary to conduct business.  While 
the Committee will seek to operate by consensus, a simple majority of a quorum will 
control on any matters requiring a vote.

<!-- page 631 -->
3 
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
3.) ADVISORY MEMBERS OF COMMITTEE 
The voting members of the Committee will appoint three additional advisory members to the 
committee.  Ideally, the advisory members will consist of one representative of a behavioral 
health agency in the northern part of Navajo County, one representative of a behavioral 
health agency in the southern part of Navajo County, and one representative from the 
Regional Behavioral Health Authority in Navajo County.   The advisory members of the 
committee will advise the rest of the Committee as to evidence-based public health 
approaches to serving those suffering from opioid addiction.  All advisory members have no 
authority to bind or act on behalf of any of the voting members of the committee or any 
parties to this MOU.   
4.) GUIDING PRINCIPLES AND CORE ABATEMENT STRATEGIES 
In addition to the guidance provided in the One Arizona Plan, the Committee shall be 
guided by the Guiding Principles and Core Abatement Strategies advocated by the John 
Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health.   Those include: 
1. Spend money to save lives. 
Given the economic downturn, many states and localities will be tempted to use the 
dollars to fill holes in their budgets rather than expand needed programs. 
Jurisdictions should use the funds to supplement rather than replace existing 
spending. 
2. Use evidence to guide spending. 
At this point in the overdose epidemic, researchers and clinicians have built a 
substantial body of evidence demonstrating what works and what does not. States and 
localities should use this information to make funding decisions. 
3. Invest in youth prevention. 
States and localities should support children, youth, and families by making long-
term investments in effective programs and strategies for community change. 
4. Focus on racial equity. 
States and localities should direct significant funds to communities affected by years 
of discriminatory policies and now experiencing substantial increases in overdoses. 
5. Develop a fair and transparent process for deciding where to spend the 
funding. 
This process should be guided by public health leaders with the active engagement of 
people and families with lived experience, clinicians, as well as other key groups.   
 
5.) CORE ABATEMENT STRATEGIES 
The Committee will strive to follow nine core abatement strategies recommended by the 
John Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health: 
A.)  Broaden access to naloxone; 
B.) Increase use of medications to treat opioid use disorder; 
C.) Provide treatment and supports during pregnancy and the postpartum period;

<!-- page 632 -->
4 
 
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
D.) The advisory members of the committee will advise the rest of the Committee 
as to evidence-based public health approaches to serving those suffering from 
opioid addiction and neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome; 
E.) Fund warm hand-off programs and recovery services; 
F.) Improve treatment in jails and prisons; 
G.) Enrich prevention strategies; 
H.) Expand harm reduction programs; 
I.) Support data collection and research. 
 
6.) TERM OF AGREEMENT 
 
This Agreement shall continue in effect so long as the Parties hereto anticipate receiving 
settlement monies pursuant to the One Arizona Plan or so long as there are still 
settlement monies available to expend on opioid remediation, whichever period is longer.  
The Agreement may further be terminated as to any municipality that is a party hereto in 
the event it decides to accept responsibility for the expenditure of One Arizona Plan 
proceeds allocated to it pursuant to the Plan and also accepts responsibility for reporting 
its expenditures of said proceeds to the Navajo County Public Health Services District 
consistent with Plan requirements. 
 
7.) EFFECTIVE DATE 
 
This Agreement shall become effective on the date it has been approved by the governing 
body of each Principal and been signed by all the Principals. 
 
8.) CANCELLATION OF AGREEMENT:  This Agreement is subject to cancellation 
subject to the provisions of A.R.S. § 38-511. 
 
9.) ENTIRE AGREEMENT:  The Principals acknowledge to one another that the terms of 
this Agreement constitute the entire understanding and Agreement of the Principal and 
Subscriber organizations regarding the matter of the Agreement. 
 
10.) INTEGRATION:  Each Principal acknowledges and agrees that it has not relied 
upon any statements, representations, agreements or warranties, except as expressed in 
this Agreement, and that this Agreement constitutes the Principals’ entire agreement with 
respect to the matters addressed in this document. All prior or contemporaneous 
agreements and understandings, oral or written, with respect to such matters are 
superseded and merged into this Agreement. This Agreement may be modified or 
amended only by written agreement signed by or for the Principals and any modification 
or amendment will become effective on the date so specified.  
 
11.) MODIFICATION:  This Agreement may be modified at any time upon the 
mutual written consent of all the then current principal organizations.

12.) SEVERABILITY:  If a court of competent jurisdiction renders any provision of 
this Agreement (or any portion of a provision) to be invalid or otherwise unenforceable, 
that provision or portion of the provision will be severed and the remainder of this 
Agreement will continue in full force and effect as if the invalid provision or portion 
thereof were not part of this Agreement. 
 
13.) COUNTERPARTS:  This Agreement may be executed in several counterparts, 
each of which shall be an original, and all of which shall constitute but one and the same

Proposed Opioid Settlement Agreement Funding Project Information Form 
Navajo County Guiding Principles 
Opioid Settlement Agreement funding is a limited opportunity to invest in the quality of life and to enhance opportunities 
by funding transformational projects and programs to improve the health of those directly impacted by the opioid epidemic 
in Navajo County. 
• Goals:  Identify and remove barriers that limit positive and healthy prevention & recovery in our communities 
• Guiding Principles 
✓ Spend money to save lives 
▪ Supplement rather than supplant existing funding 
▪ Don’t spend all the money at once or on one initiative 
▪ Report to the public where the money is being spent & measures to determine success 
✓ Use evidence to guide spending 
o Direct funds to programs supported by evidence 
o Remove polices that may block adoption of programs that work 
o Build data collection capacity 
✓ Invest in youth prevention 
o Direct funds to evidence-based or evidence-informed interventions 
✓ Focus on racial equality 
o Invest in communities affected by discriminatory polices 
o Support diversion from arrest & incarceration 
o Fund anti-stigma campaigns 
o Involve community members in solutions, including those with lived experience 
✓ Develop a fair & transparent process for deciding where to spend the funding 
o Determine areas of greatest need 
o Receive input from groups that touch different parts of the epidemic to develop the plan 
o Ensure representation that reflects the diversity of affected communities when allocating 
funds

Title: Contract B23-02-024 Supply of Aggregate for Cover Materials
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Stevie Studer, Account Specialist
Department: Public Works
Presented By: Madhav Mundle
Motion before the Board:
Consideration of award of Contract Number B23-02-024, Supply of Aggregate for Cover
Material to Perkins Cinders Inc, Hatch Construction and Paving Inc, and Brimhall Sand Rock
and Building Materials, effective April 11, 2023, through April 10, 2024.
Background:
The purpose of these annual contracts is to supply Navajo County's road maintenance operation
with the aggregate rock material used for chip seal projects as part of its preventive
maintenance program.  Awarding contracts to multiple local vendors who provide material at
multiple locations throughout the County is operationally and financially beneficial to the
County.  
Sealed proposals were received by the Board of Supervisors at the Navajo County Government
Center, Holbrook, Arizona until 3:00 p.m. M.S.T., March 30, 2023 in strict accordance with
specifications on file in the office of the Navajo County Department of Public Works.  No bids
were accepted after 3:00 p.m. M.S.T.  The bids were publicly opened and read aloud at 3:15 p.m.
Navajo County may award contracts to all bidders for each item and select the bidder at the time
of purchase based on price, convenience, availability, and/or quality.  Three bids were received
with an average cost increase of 1.62% for materials (excluding hauling) compared to last year. 
The award of contracts to all bidders allows adequate coverage for materials by location. 
Recommendation: 
Staff recommends approval.

approving/denying a Special Use Permit to operate a recovery residential facility for ten (10)
residents with 13 staff per week with overlapping shifts.
Background:
The property is 5 acres with an existing structure used to be utilized as a nursing home. APN#
409-25-003B, T10N, R21E, S09.  Owner:  Pine Top Holdings, LLC.  Agent: Onkar Bhowra.
The applicant, Sunrise Health and Recovery (SHR) is requesting approval of a Special Use
Permit to operate a licensed Behavioral Health Residential Facility (BHRF) at 965 Full House
Lane in the Linden area.
Staff included the staff report prepared for the Planning and Zoning Commission and all the
attachments provided by the applicant for the supervisors' review. 
On January 19, 2023, after hearing applicants' presentation, neighbors', school district's and
parents' comments, the P&Z Commission unanimously voted to recommend denial of the
request to the Board of Supervisors. 
 
Recommendation: 
If the Board of Supervisors approve the Special Use Permit on APN# 409-25-003B, staff
recommends the following conditions: 
The permitted Special Use shall allow maximum of 10 residents at the facility.1.
The Fire Department requirements shall be met at all times.2.
No building or structure shall not be occupied prior to complete compliance with all
appropriate Building Department requirements.
3.
All lighting on the property shall be shielded to reflect downward, be motion-activated,
and be in conformance with the Navajo County Lighting Ordinance.
4.
The permitted Special Use shall be allowed to occur per the attached/approved site plan. 
Any expansion or change of the Special Use shall require an amendment to this Permit.
5.
This Special Use Permit shall run with the land pending compliance with all County,6.

State, and Federal requirements.

date of Board approval, this permit shall become null and void.

STAFF REPORT  
 
 
 
TO: Planning and Zoning Commission 
 
FROM: Berrin Nejad, Community Development Director 
  
HEARING DATE: January 19, 2023   
 
PROJECT NUMBER:   SUP 22 -010 SUNRISE HEALTH and RECOVERY 
RESIDENTIAL FACILITY, DISTRICT IV: A request for a Special 
Use Permit to operate a recovery residential facility for ten (10) 
residents with 13 staff per week with overlapping shifts. The property 
is 5 acres with an existing structure used to be utilized as a nursing 
home. APN# 409-25-003B, T10N, R21E, S09.  Owner:  Pine Top 
Holdings, LLC.  Agent: Onkar Bhowra. 
 
 
 
BACKGROUND and ANALYSIS: 
The applicant, Sunrise Health and Recovery (SHR) is requesting approval of a Special Use Permit 
to operate a licensed Behavioral Health Residential Facility (BHRF) at 965 Full House Lane in the 
Linden area.  
 
The site is located on Full House Lane from SR 260 and there is an existing building, which used to 
function as a nursing home  in the past.  There is a school facility at the southeast corner of the SR 
260 and Full House.  The subject property is located kitty corner from the school.  The school 
property and the residential use on the north side are zoned C-R, Commercial-Residential, the rear, 
the south and cross the street properties are residential uses with A-General zoning.  
 
 
Adjacent Land Use and Zoning: 
 
  North  C-R Residential Use 
  South  A-General Residential Use 
  East  A-General Residential Use 
  West   A-General Residential Use (across the Full House Lane)

<!-- page 650 -->
Planning and Zoning Commission                                     January 19, 2023        2 | P a g e  
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
 
SHR is currently licensed by the State of Arizona - Arizona Department of Health Services  and is 
administered by Dr. Nathan A. Velez to serve Navajo County residents in the White Mountains. The 
license is to operate a 10-bed facility at this location. The operational protocol is stated as follows:  
 
• Audible alarms on all doors and windows that sound when opened. 
• Hourly (or less, as required) rounds to ensure all patients/residents are on site. 
• Prohibit the admission of individuals with a history of sex crimes 
• Prohibit the admission of individuals on the sexual abuse registry 
• Prohibit the use of alcohol or drugs on site 
• Discharge of residents who test positive for alcohol or drugs while in treatment 
• Extensive staff training in safety measures to include verbal de-escalation of altercations 
• Staff member/s are in-house, and awake, 24 hours a day / 7 days a week. 
• Comprehensive therapy for all residents, to include individual, group and family, as well as 12-
step, daily living and Wellbriety sessions. 
• Facility is monitored inside and out with security cameras 24 hours a day / 7 days a week 
• Outside recreational area is fenced to allow freedom of movement within a prescribed area only 
• Random / weekly urine tests on residents for illicit substances. 
 
 
Following information is provided in the narrative by the applicant:  
 
Number of Residents: 
The number of residents at Sunrise Health and Recovery residential facility will  be 10, as licensed 
by Arizona Department of Health Services (ADHS.) 
 
 Length of Stay: 
• The residential program length of stay is determined according to medical need criteria per 
The American Society of Addiction Medicine criteria. All applicants requesting residential 
treatment will be required to complete a Pre-Screen, Inquiry and if eligible an intake followed

Zoning Ordinance: Navajo County, Zoning Ordinance addresses Manufactured Home Parks in the 
following areas:  
 
ARTICLE 15 – (C-R) COMMERCIAL-RESIDENTIAL ZONING DISTRICT 
Section 1501 – Purpose  
The principal purpose of this zoning district is to provide for shops and services in convenient 
locations to meet the daily needs of families in the immediate residential neighborhoods and 
wholesaling or distribution activities in locations where there is adequate access to major streets or 
highways.  Principal uses permitted in this zoning district include retail and wholesale commerce, 
commercial entertainment, and some uses of a light manufacturing nature. 
 
 
ZONING ORDINANCE: 
Article 20 – Special Uses and Planned Unit Developments 
 
Section 2001 – Special Uses 
The Board of Supervisors may permit as a Special Use the following uses in zoning districts from 
which they are otherwise prohibited by this Ordinance, unless any such use is further prohibited by 
this Article. 
 
18. Institutional Residential and other Group Homes. 
 
 
Article 25- General Provisions, Section 2518: 
Section 2518 – Group Homes for the Disabled 
1. Purpose:   The purpose of these regulations is to permit disabled persons, as defined by state 
and federal law, to reside in single-family residences in compliance with the Fair Housing Act 
and Arizona state law, while maintaining the residential character of neighborhoods. 
2. Applicability. 
a. Zoning Confirmation: Prior to registration, requests for zoning c onfirmation may be 
submitted to the Planning and Zoning Department to confirm the proposed location of 
the group home is permitted per this Section. 
b. Additional Requirements of State Law: Notwithstanding the foregoing, if the State has 
adopted laws or rules  for the regulation of a specific type of home, such as a Group 
Home for the Developmentally Disabled or an Assisted Living Home as defined by state 
statutes, then any such State law or rule shall apply in addition to the conditions listed 
herein and shall preempt any conflicting condition listed herein. 
 
3. Performance Standards:  Group Homes for the Disabled shall be located, developed, and 
operated in compliance with the following standards:

<!-- page 656 -->
Planning and Zoning Commission                                     January 19, 2023        8 | P a g e  
Navajo County - For Official Use Only 
a. Separation: The minimum separation between group homes shall be 1,200 feet as 
prescribed by A.R.S. § 36-582, as measured by the closest property lines. 
b. Occupancy: The number of residents, excluding staff, shall not exceed 10. 
c. Exterior Appearance: There shall be no sign or other exterior indication of a group 
home visible from a street. 
d. Compliance with Building, Environmental Health, and Fire Safety Regulations: Group 
homes shall be required to comply with all relevant building, environmental health, 
and fire safety regulations.  If a group home has one or more non-ambulatory residents, 
building code requirements in addition to those applicable to group homes containing 
no non-ambulatory residents, shall apply. 
e. Licensing: Group homes shall comply with applicable licensing requirements. 
f. Parking: Any parking for the group homes shall be on site. 
 
4. Permits and Administration. 
a. Property is considered a Group Home for the Disabled under this Ordinance after the 
Navajo County Planning and Zoning Department issues a Permit for a Group Home 
for the Disabled for that property.  Only properties serving occupants who fit the 
definition of disabled under the Fair Housing Act are eligible for determination as a 
Group Home for the Disabled. 
b. In order to secure a permit for a group home for the disabled, an application must be 
submitted on t he form prescribed by the Planning and Zoning Department.  The 
application must include the following: 
i. A site plan 
ii. A notarized statement detailing qualifications 
iii. Copies of applicable licenses  
iv. Affidavit of compliance and other documentation indicating the property 
as a group home for the disabled 
v. Any additional information or plans, if deemed necessary 
 
c. If standards are not met, the home shall be considered another group home or 
institutional residential use and shall be subject to the provisions of the Zon ing 
Ordinance guiding such establishments.  Status as a Group Home for the Disabled is 
open to review by the Navajo County Planning and Zoning Department and may be 
cancelled at any time upon a determination by the Director that the property is no 
longer b eing used for a qualifying purpose or meeting standards laid forth in this 
Ordinance.

A “Project Narrative” (2 copies), expressing your reasons for the proposed Special 
Use Permit and how it will be beneficial to the area, and including an explanation of 
the proposed use, a schedule for its development, and the compatibility of the 
proposed use with the adjacent uses and character of the area 
 
Sunrise Health and Recovery (SHR) seeks to operate under a Special Use Permit a Licensed 
Behavioral Health Residential Facility (BHRF). SHR is currently licensed by the State of 
Arizona-Arizona Department of Health Services and meets all registered criteria for such use.  
SHR seeks to operate in the Show Low, Arizona area as there is a high demand and 
concentrate of Substance Use/Misuse, Opiate Use Dependence and published material in the 
local Navajo County Press about a need for treatment facilities to assist in this epidemic. 
According the 2020 Navajo County Overdose Fatality Review (Attached) key factors identified 
included improved “access to care” in the immediate area, an increase of Medication Assisted 
Treatment (MAT) in the area, “improved coordination of care” between hospitals, jails and 
treatment facilities. Additionally, it is noted that “South County” of Navajo (Snowflake, Taylor, 
Show Low) are were most prevalent cases of Opiate Overdose fatalities occur. As such, 
Fentanyl accounted for 48% and Alcohol 32% of all overdoses in Navajo County, both carry 
potential lethal overdose potential. SHR and its leadership believes this is a very beneficial 
opportunity to both the local Navajo County area and greater Navajo County Region. Providing 
a service to save lives and enhance recovery places residents back into our community as 
contributors to our local communities and reduces crime, increases employment and keeps 
families united.  
 
SHR is administered by a long-time local Navajo County Resident, Dr. Nathan A. Velez, Phd, 
LPC, LPC who served in a decade long capacity both as a treatment provider and Deputy 
Probation Officer to Navajo County. Dr. Velez identifies this use of a BHRF in the Show Low 
area can be of service to not only all of Navajo County Residents, but specifically target the area 
affected the most. It is Dr. Velez’s passion to serve the residents of Navajo County, in this 
particular area as he describes “far too often our people of Navajo County are having to leave 
the area or state to get much needed treatment, often leaving their community and families, who 
are essential to the healing and change process.” As a part of recovery and treatment, “it is 
essential to heal within the community.” In addition, the SHR Center is Directed Clinically by a 
local Substance Abuse Recovery Expert, and longtime Navajo County resident and recovery 
advocate, Eugene “Ed” Gonzales. Ed has served the Navajo County community for over 30 
years in the helping profession and eagerly awaits to help service in the capacity of Clinical 
Director of SHR to ensure our people of Navajo County obtain the best evidenced based care. 
Mr. Gonzales, also was instrumental in starting Navajo County Drug Court over 1 decade ago 
with now presiding Judge Dale Nielsen and C.A. Brad Carylon. His passion for helping those in 
recovery is a blessing to the communities of Navajo County. In short, between Dr. Velez and Mr. 
Gonzales, a combined 60 years of experience servicing the communities of Navajo County 
Exist.  
The schedule for development is a Grand Opening to the public to be of transparency and to 
allow the community to visit and see the elements of the treatment center. It is of tremendous 
importance for SHR to be a part of the community, while operating within the community. The

<!-- page 665 -->
parcel of land and privacy of the location of the facility also serves tremendous purpose for 
those who are healing and in recovery. The connection to nature, privacy from the city and 
ability to focus on their care are essential to the residents of Navajo County in recovery. The 
location provides the ability to and opportunity to heal in nature. Thus, our slogan, “Recovery in 
the Pines.” Attached you will find our website for additional information and questions: 
www.sunrisehealthandrecovery.com. You will also find a list of stakeholders who are supportive 
of the BHRF to include the local criminal justice sector leaders (Navajo County Probation and 
County Attorney) Jason Cash and Brad Carlyon, Blue Cross Blue Shield CEO and President 
Shawn NAU (Northern Az Medicaid Plan) and many others.  
 
SHR appreciates the concerns that may be expressed by the community in regards to the 
location of our facility and the type of residents SHR proposes to serve.  SHR has taken multiple 
steps to ensure the safety of the community, staff and residents.  To that end, SHR has 
implemented the following protocols and safety measures: 
 Audible alarms on all doors and windows that sound when opened. 
 Hourly (or less, as required) rounds to ensure all patients/residents are on site. 
 Prohibit the admission of individuals with a history of sex crimes 
 Prohibit the admission of individuals on the sexual abuse registry 
 Prohibit the use of alcohol or drugs on site 
 Discharge of residents who test positive for alcohol or drugs while in treatment 
 Extensive staff training in safety measures to include verbal de-escalation of altercations 
 Staff member/s are in-house, and awake, 24 hours a day / 7 days a week.  
 Comprehensive therapy for all residents, to include individual, group and family, as well 
as 12-step, daily living and Wellbriety sessions. 
 Facility is monitored inside and out with security cameras 24 hours a day / 7 days a 
week 
 Outside recreational area is fenced to allow freedom of movement within a prescribed 
area only 
 Random / weekly urine tests on residents for illicit substances 
 
SHR believes that by taking the above measures, it can best mitigate the concerns of the 
surrounding community and ensure the safety of all involved.

General Description: Sunrise Health and Recovery, LLC (SHR) is licensed to operate as a 10 bed Behavioral Health 
Residential Facility (RTC). SHR specializes in treating chemical abuse/dependency, and other addictive and mental health 
disorders. SHR continuum of care begins with a focus on identifying and treating the underlying causal conditions that 
lead to Substance Use and Abuse (SUD’s) addictive behavior; transitioning individuals into sustaining a Wellness 
Recovery Action Plan (WRAP), to achieve a sustainable long term, hopeful for a lifetime in a Recovery Lifestyle.  
 
Sunrise Health and Recovery offers a cost and individualized effective solutions for adult men and women who struggle 
with addiction and chronic relapse.  SHR will provide services for people that will need a continuum of care beyond the 
traditional 30-60 days of residential care. Our belief is that by offering a safe and nurturing therapeutic environment, the 
client will be able to have a variety of controlled experiences which will allow them to find their own path to long term 
wellness in sobriety and growth.  
 
SHR encompasses dignity and respect in an environment designed to be culturally sensitive, provide evidenced based 
program modalities, which incorporate a faceted focus on the individual to build confidence, self worth, esteem and the 
knowledge and wisdom to make better choices for self, family and community. Overall, the SHR Program emphasizes 
wellness in life:  
 MATRIX, a Cognitive Behavioral Therapy, a modality of substance use disorder treatment, as a psychological 
treatment demonstrated to be effective in a range of problems including depression, anxiety disorders, alcohol 
and drug use problems, marital problems, eating disorders and severe mental illness, 
 
 WELLBRIETY, achieving sobriety and abstinence from substance abuse and misuse without stopping there. It 
means going beyond “clean and sober” by entering a journey of healing and balance - mentally, physically, 
emotionally and spiritually. 
 
 SAMSHA: Eight Dimensions of Wellness: SAMHSA's Wellness Initiative supports embracing the Eight 
Dimensions of Wellness: emotional, environmental, financial, intellectual, occupational, physical, social, and 
spiritual to achieve longevity in learned Recovery Lifestyle changes and improved quality of life. 
 
 VIA Character Strengths Classifications: With these criteria of observed six main virtues that emerged in 
societies across the world and across time. Within each of these virtues are several characters strengths that relate to 
displaying or enacting the virtue: Wisdom and Knowledge: Creativity, Curiosity, Open-mindedness, Love of 
learning, Perspective; Courage: Bravery, Persistence, Integrity, Vitality; Humanity: Love, Kindness, Social 
intelligence; Justice: Citizenship, Fairness, Leadership; Moderation/Temperance: Forgiveness and mercy, 
Humility/Modesty, Prudence, Self-regulation; Transcendence: Appreciation of beauty and excellence, Gratitude, 
Hope/Optimism, Humor, Spirituality and ZEST. 
 
  Medication-assisted treatment (MAT) is used to treat substance use disorders as well as sustain recovery and 
prevent overdose. All entering will be assessed with a Psychiatric Evaluation; Medical Team will monitor. 
 
SHR will introduce 12 step model(s) for a strong emphasis on individual involvement.  Provide a strong focus on social 
responsibility and independent living skills. SHR’s continuum care is monitored by Clinical and Medical Teams.  Our 
EMR is Lightning Step Software, which provides: Best Practices Documentation, Real-time Data Access, Flexible & 
Powerful Reporting, Managed Care, Performance Outcomes, Billing/Daily Scheduling, and Security/Privacy (HIPAA) 
 
SHR staffs are licensed behavioral health professionals or behavior health technicians under the direct supervision of a 
behavior health professional.  Progression is based on the client’s ability to successfully accomplish goals, to meet

Dear Navajo County Board of Supervisors and Planning and Zoning Commissioners, 
As a 30-year resident of Navajo County, I have seen the horrible effects of substance use 
and how it escalated further during the pandemic. I know many individuals who lost 
their lives or a family member due to this disease. 
Based on data from the 2020 CHNA update, alcohol/drug use is the seventh most 
common primary reason for a hospital stay and is involved in more than 2,000 hospital 
stays as the primary or other reason for the visit for Navajo County residents. Alcohol 
deaths in Navajo County continued to rise from 65.9 per 100,000 in 2017 to 71.8 in 
2019. Four times the Arizona average of 17.6 (Navajo County CHNA 2020). 
Too often, drugs and alcohol are used to self-medicate co-occurring mental health issues 
brought on by trauma, mostly childhood (i.e., poverty, neglect, physical and sexual 
abuse). In 2019 there were almost 600 hospital stays by Navajo County residents related 
to suicides, suicide attempts, and intentional self-inflicted injuries (2020 Navajo County 
CHNA update). 
Recently I was notified that the Arizona Department of Health Services had approved a 
License for Sunrise Health and Recovery to operate a ten-bed Behavioral Health 
Residential Treatment Facility (RTC) at 965 Full House Rd in Linden. As I understand 
and support, the program will provide a higher level of treatment for individuals with 
chemical use/dependency and other substance and mental health disorders. 
As I have been made aware, Sunrise Health and Recovery care focuses on therapy, has a 
Medical Team to provide medication-assisted treatment, Licensed Professional 
Therapist, and skilled Support Specialists to provide 24 hours a day services and 
coverage. 
Our residents need RECOVERY; to achieve and maintain recovery, we must focus on 
TREATMENT! I support addressing the need to offer help and support for individuals 
suffering from substance use seeking recovery, the opportunity to develop and achieve 
therapy to sustain a long-term, 100% substance free individualized Recovery Lifestyle. 
With my support, I encourage Sunrise Health and Recovery the ability to be granted the 
“Special Permit.” 
Sincerely, 
Allison Hephner 
ah@cpmsaz.com 
928-243-1332

PETITION 
The undersigned persons respectfully request that the Navajo County Planning and Zoning 
Commission recommend, and if recommended, the Board of Supervisors grant request for 
Special Use Permit 22-010 Sunrise Health and recovery Residential Facility District IV regarding 
APN #409-25-003B for the following reasons: 
1. Sunrise Health and Recovery (SHR) Residential Treatment Center (RTC) is licensed to 
operate a 10-bed residential facility by the Arizona Department of Health Services.  This 
facility will provide 30-, 60-, or 90-day in-house treatment to individuals recovering from 
substance abuse disorders.  
2. Listed below are facts and accurate data regarding the proposed use of the facility: 
a. Addiction is a Disease; alcoholics and/or addicts are sick; SHR offers life-saving therapy 
services. 
b. Our property is secured with all doors locked; internal/external surveillance cameras 
are monitored. 
c. Fully trained personnel provide 24-hour supervision, 7 days a week. 
d. Clinical and Medical Teams will assess, evaluate and develop treatment based on 
Medical Need. 
e. Referrals are by phone, admissions arrive for placement; sober/clean from 
detox/hospital, community. 
f. No gatherings/congregating will be tolerated on property. 
g. Clients will remain indoors at all times, only allowed out the back on the fenced 
patio/property. 
h. Admissions, supplies delivered, and staff parking will only be allowed on the parking 
lot. 
i. Individuals of suspect, wandering the neighborhood, will not be enrolled at our facility; 
decisions to contact local authorities will be made for safety interventions. 
j. SHR offers individuals and their families the opportunity to heal in “Wellness” with 
therapeutic services 
k. Our Goal: develop and sustain the opportunity to live 100% substance free; long term 
Recovery Lifestyle. 
l. SHR held an Open House on Sept. 1,2022, which was highly attended with positive 
feedback from neighbors and community. 
m. Our Clinical Program Director has 30+ years as an Administrator and Clinical Director; 
SHR is his 7th residential/outpatient clinic.  He is an addict in recovery with 34 Years 
34 Years Sober/Clean.  
n. Safety is always the #1 priority. 
o. With Dignity and Respect, approval of the “Special Permit,” is one step towards a 
SOLUTION to treat substance abuse, use, and disorders in the White Mountains.

RESOLUTION ____-23 
 
A RESOLUTION OF THE NAVAJO COUNTY BOARD OF SUPERVISORS APPROVING 
A SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR SUNRISE HEALTH AND RECOVERY RESIDENTIAL 
FACILITY. 
 
WHEREAS, an application for a Special Use Permit  was duly filed on  November 03, 
2022 by Onkar Bhowra to operate Sunrise Health and Recovery Residential Facility; and 
 
WHEREAS, the application concerns the following real property in Navajo County:  
APN# 409-25-003B, T10N, R21E, S09; and 
 
WHEREAS, the application was considered by the Navajo County Planning & Zoning 
Commission at a duly noticed public hearing on January 19, 2023; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Navajo County Board of Supervis ors after considering the testimony 
and other evidence presented at the hearing, as well a s the recommendations of staff, found that 
the Special Use Permit is consistent with the public health, safety and general welfare and should 
be approved; and 
 
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT R ESOLVED the Board of Superviso rs hereby 
approve the Special Use Permit, subject to the following conditions: 
 
1. The permitted Special Use shall allow maximum of 10 residents at the facility.  
2. The Fire Department requirements shall be met at all times.  
3. No building or structure shall not be occupied prior to complete compliance with all 
appropriate Building Department requirements. 
4. All lighting on the property shall be shielded to reflect downward, be motion -activated, 
and be in conformance with the Navajo County Lighting Ordinance. 
5. The permitted Special Use shall be allowed to occur per the attached/approved  site plan.  
Any expansion or change of the Special Use shall require an amendment to this Permit. 
6. This Special Use Permit shall run with the land pending compliance with all County, 
State, and Federal requirements.   
7. If the permitted Special Use is not ut ilized within a twelve (1 2) month period, from the 
date of Board approval, this permit shall become null and void.

A SPECIAL USE PERMIT FOR SUNRISE HEALTH AND RECOVERY RESIDENTIAL 
FACILITY. 
 
WHEREAS, an application for a Special Use Permit  was duly filed on  November 03, 
2022 by Onkar Bhowra to operate Sunrise Health and Recovery Residential Facility; and 
 
WHEREAS, the application concerns the following real property in Navajo County:  
APN# # 409-25-003B, T10N, R21E, S09; and 
 
WHEREAS, the application was considered by the Navajo County Planning & Zoning 
Commission at a duly noticed public hearing on January 19, 2023; and 
 
WHEREAS, the Navajo County Board of Supervis ors after considering the testimony 
and other evidence presented at the hearing, as well a s the recommendations of staff, found that 
the Special Use Permit is not consistent with the public health, safety and general welfare and 
should be denied; and 
 
NOW, THEREFORE BE IT R ESOLVED the Board of Super visors hereby 
deny the Special Use Permit.

Board of Supervisors Regular 9. c. 1. a.        
Meeting Date: 04/11/2023  
Title: Bourdon Ranch Road, Millet Swale Culverts Amendment No. 1 Dist. III
Submitted For: Madhav Mundle, Public Works Director 
Submitted By: Jeanine Carruthers, Deputy Director Administration
Department: Public Works
Motion before the Board:
Amendment Number 1 to the Professional Services Agreement with The WLB Group, Inc. for
the Bourdon Ranch Road / Millet Swale Culvert Project
Background:
On March 8, 2022, the Board of Directors approved a contract with The WLB Group for the
amount of $88,095 to prepare engineering construction plans for replacing the existing (3)
corrugated metal pipes (CPM) with multiple larger capacity Culverts to increase the drainage
flow capacity under Bourdon Ranch Road.  Amendment No. 1 adds additional services to the
agreement to include a geotechnical evaluation report to base the final culvert and headwall
foundation system design.  These services will increase the contract amount by an additional
seven thousand nine hundred thirty five dollars for a total amount not to exceed ninety-six
thousand thirty dollars.
Fiscal Impact
Fiscal Year: FY 2023
Budgeted Y/N: Y
Amount Requested:
Fiscal Impact:
Funds are budgeted in the FY 2023 and FY 2024 budgets.

Re: Bourdon Ranch Road / Millet Swale Culverts Additional Service Request 1 - Added Geotechnical Evaluation 
WLB No.: 322008A001 
Dear Mr. Flake, 
Based upon preliminary design options for the new culvert system, it was determined that the County and 
project would best be served by obtaining a geotechnical evaluation report to base the final culvert and 
headwall foundation system designs on. 
At the request of the County, WLB added a geotechnical subconsultant, Western Technologies Inc., to provide 
a geotechnical evaluation for the project.  WLB coordinated the scope and timing of the geotechnical work 
with both WTI and the County, including WTI providing necessary traffic control due to the scheduled work 
availability occurring on a County holiday. 
Per coordination, this change order is to cover the cost of the geotechnical evaluation and report services as a 
reimbursable expense for WLB on the project.  Further geotechnical services beyond the field evaluation and 
geotechnical evaluation report, should they be requested, may be additional services that would be scope at 
the appropriate times.  The detailed geotechnical scope can be found in the WTI proposals attached to this 
Additional Service Request. 
COMPENSATION:   
Our proposed reimbursable expense for the Additiona l Service Request 1 – Added Geotechnical Evaluation  is 
$7,935  including WLB’s standard 15% markup.  Per prior coordination with the County, the base fees for the WTI 
geotechnical services and the traffic control are $5,900 and $1,000, respectively.  The breakdown of the budget 
is presented in the following table:  
 
Additional Services 
Reimbursable Expenses 
Western Technologies (Geotechnical Evaluation) $7,935 
Total Additional Services $7,935   
 
We will bill monthly for services provided. Additional services authorized by the client will be billed monthly.
